assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single polymer molecules electrically as they thread a nanopore is a clean physical principle (ionic current blockade) converted into a transformative capability: long-read, label-free DNA and RNA sequencing. Combines originality, quantitative engineering and broad downstream impact in genomics.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived strand-through-pore detection, Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation in alpha-hemolysin, Bayley engineered protein pores and Akeson established enzyme-controlled ratcheting. The ratchet step is decisive for sequencing, but the credit is spread over five people and I cannot cleanly resolve which three fit best; my trio is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: Commercial nanopore sequencing has been in widespread use for roughly a decade, with independent confirmation across many labs and applications. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among conception, demonstration, protein-pore engineering and motor-enzyme control is genuinely contested.
I have not verified current status of all credited individuals, which may constrain the trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell brings a physical-chemistry concept (condensation, thermodynamics of multivalent interactions) to explain compartmentalization without membranes. It reshaped cell biology and opened questions in disease and design.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule demonstration by Brangwynne and Hyman is the founding observation, and Rosen's multivalent-interaction work supplied the quantitative chemical framework. Pappu and Mittag are important on sequence grammar and theory, but a Hyman-Brangwynne-Rosen trio is a defensible core.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is broad, but there is active debate about which cellular condensates are truly phase-separated versus other assemblies, and about functional relevance in vivo. Slightly early for a clean, conflict-free citation.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance and over claims that are really descriptive.
Whether the prize would be seen as chemistry or physiology/medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one nucleotide to another without double-strand breaks, a chemically conceived solution that opened precise genome editing with enormous therapeutic and research potential, and has reached clinical use.
assessment.attribution: Liu was the intellectual driver of both cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees and Nishida and Kondo reported an independent cytidine deaminase approach. A single-laureate proposal fits Liu's decisive role, though a prize might prefer to group it with prime editing under one citation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials and approvals are now emerging with strong independent validation. Timely, with some risk that the CRISPR prize in 2020 makes the committee wary of a second genome-editing prize.
uncertainties: Committee appetite for another genome-editing prize after 2020.
Treatment of the Nishida/Kondo parallel work and of prime editing in the same citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers rose from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency within a decade, a striking materials discovery with obvious relevance to energy. The physics of defect tolerance and long carrier diffusion are compelling.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites in a sensitized cell (2009), Park and collaborators made the first solid-state high-efficiency cell (2012), and Snaith's group showed the mesosuperstructured and planar architectures. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also contributed materially, so the trio omits major figures.
assessment.maturity: Remarkable efficiency progress is confirmed, but stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain open, so recognition could be seen as premature.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and scale-up are unresolved.
Crowded credit; the 2009 origin is a low-efficiency liquid-cell result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to hijack ubiquitin ligases for targeted degradation is a new pharmacological modality that acts catalytically rather than by occupancy. It is conceptually original and now widespread in drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept (2001), Crews drove its development, and Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and structural design; Handa, Ito and others uncovered how thalidomide-type molecular glues work through cereblon. The compound of PROTACs and molecular glues may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Many compounds are in clinical trials but approval of a PROTAC is still pending, so validation is incomplete; the molecular glue branch is more mature.
uncertainties: Absence of an approved PROTAC drug.
Whether PROTACs and glue degraders belong in one citation, and who is credited for each.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated programmable folding of nanoscale objects with addressable features and spawned a field of molecular nanotechnology, with clear design principles and impressive precision.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami paper is the decisive invention, building on Seeman's structural DNA nanotechnology, who is not on the list; this omission weakens the prize configuration. Yin and Shih extended the approach to 3D, tiles and bricks, though their contributions are more incremental.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated and widely adopted, but practical applications beyond research tools remain limited, and the foundational contributor from the earlier era is not creditable here.
uncertainties: Missing foundational credit and the question whether a fair configuration exists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Orbitrap converts a purely physical idea, image-current detection of ions oscillating in an electrostatic trap, into a high-resolution mass analyzer that is now ubiquitous in proteomics, metabolomics and analytical chemistry. A clear physical principle with measurable performance.
assessment.attribution: Makarov is the sole inventor credited and is decisive for the realisation; the earlier Kingdon trap concept is background. A single-laureate prize is possible but an enabling-instrument citation could be bundled with proteomics.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with two decades of independent use and confirmation. Timely, though instrument prizes in chemistry typically need a paired scientific application.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would give a single-inventor instrument prize.
Role of the company in the development is not documented in the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials give near first-principles accuracy at classical cost, a new capability for simulating reactions and materials at scale. The generative potential is high and the work is broadly adopted.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's neural-network potentials (2007) and Bartók and Csányi's Gaussian approximation potentials (2010) are the core, with Parrinello also central to other computational methods; I would pick Behler, Parrinello and Csányi, leaving out Bartók, which is a difficult call.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving field, with foundation models superseding earlier methods; an early prize might favour a moving target.
uncertainties: The field is still evolving and the lasting contribution may shift.
Credit is split between multiple frameworks and Bartók's role is arguably equal to Csányi's.
